chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far and Abi 'Abdillah عليهما السلام, that they both said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform wudu (ablution) with one mudd and perform ghusl (ritual bath) with one sa'.” Then he said:
“He and his wife performed ghusl with five mudds from a single vessel.”

Zurarah said: So I said to him, “How did he do that?” He said: “He began, so he dipped his hand into the water before her and cleaned his private part. Then she dipped and cleaned her private part. Then he poured water over himself and she poured water over herself until they finished. So the amount with which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله performed ghusl was three mudds, and that with which she performed ghusl was two mudds. It only sufficed for them because they shared together entirely. But whoever performs ghusl alone by himself must have one sa'.”

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: plural of mudd, a unit of liquid measure
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a larger measure equal to four mudds

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for ghusl from janabah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the amount of water used for wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath), including the case where the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and his wife shared one vessel. It indicates that a reduced total amount suffices when two people share the water together, while a person performing ghusl alone requires a full sa'. The report is relevant to the fiqh of ritual purity and the practical sunnah (prophetic tradition) of bathing from janabah.
